classification.difficultyReason: Plot four specified members of a quadratic family using technology and identify their common intercepts.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Use computer graphing software to plot on the one number plane the parabola $y=a(x-1)(x-3)$ for the following values of $a$.

answer.worked:
Enter $y=2(x-1)(x-3)$ in the graphing software. The curve is concave up, with zeroes $1$ and $3$.
$$\begin{align*}y(0)&=2(0-1)(0-3)\\y(0)&=6\\y(2)&=2(2-1)(2-3)\\y(2)&=-2\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(2,-2)$. Plot this curve on the same axes as the other three.

Enter $y=(x-1)(x-3)$ in the graphing software. The curve is concave up, with zeroes $1$ and $3$.
$$\begin{align*}y(0)&=(0-1)(0-3)\\y(0)&=3\\y(2)&=(2-1)(2-3)\\y(2)&=-1\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(2,-1)$. Plot this curve on the same axes as the other three.

Enter $y=-(x-1)(x-3)$ in the graphing software. The curve is concave down, with zeroes $1$ and $3$.
$$\begin{align*}y(0)&=-(0-1)(0-3)\\y(0)&=-3\\y(2)&=-(2-1)(2-3)\\y(2)&=1\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(2,1)$. Plot this curve on the same axes as the other three.

Enter $y=-2(x-1)(x-3)$ in the graphing software. The curve is concave down, with zeroes $1$ and $3$.
$$\begin{align*}y(0)&=-2(0-1)(0-3)\\y(0)&=-6\\y(2)&=-2(2-1)(2-3)\\y(2)&=2\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(2,2)$. Plot this curve on the same axes as the other three.

spec.description: Four equation-driven parabolas on one coordinate plane, distinguished by line styles and a labelled legend.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Which two points do all these parabolas pass through?

answer.worked:
For every specified value of $a$, either factor is zero at $x=1$ or $x=3$:
$$\begin{align*}y(1)&=a(1-1)(1-3)=0\\y(3)&=a(3-1)(3-3)=0\end{align*}$$
Thus all four parabolas pass through $(1,0)$ and $(3,0)$.
